user.title: Connect to a Meshtastic node
user.description: Enter the hostname or IP address of the Meshtastic node that Home Assistant should connect to. The node must have its network API enabled and only accepts one client at a time.

data.download_node_db: Download the node database on connect

data_description.host: The hostname or IP address of the node.
data_description.port: The TCP port of the node's API. The default is 4403.
data_description.download_node_db: Ask the node for its full list of known nodes when connecting. Leave this off on memory-constrained nodes, which can crash while sending it.

reconfigure.title: Change the address of the Meshtastic node
reconfigure.description: Point Home Assistant at a new address for this node. It has to be the same node: to connect to a different one, add another entry instead.

data_description.host: The hostname or IP address of the node.

error.already_in_use: The node closed the connection. It accepts only one client at a time, so disconnect the Meshtastic app or CLI and try again.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: That address belongs to a different Meshtastic node. Please reconfigure against the same node.

data_description.include_location: Put the coordinates of every node in the diagnostics download instead of redacting them. Leave this off unless you are about to attach the download to a bug report you have read.
data_description.track_position: Create a device tracker for every node that reports a position. Turn this off to keep node positions out of the state machine entirely.

admin_not_authorized.message: {node} refused the administration request on this channel.

no_node_info.message: The node did not report its own identity.

no_radio.message: The node has no usable radio interface.

reboot_in_progress.message: {node} is already rebooting. Wait for it to come back.

circuit_breaker_open.title: Meshtastic keeps losing the connection to {name}

confirm.title: [%key:component::meshtastic::issues::circuit_breaker_open::title%]
confirm.description:
Home Assistant was disconnected from {name} at {host} {count} times in a row, so it has paused reconnecting for {seconds} seconds.

A Meshtastic node accepts a single network client at a time. This almost always means something else is holding that slot: the Meshtastic phone app, the web client, or a `meshtastic --host {host}` command left running.

Close the other client, then select **Submit** to reconnect immediately.

migrated_from_custom_integration.title: Meshtastic was carried over from the custom integration

confirm.title: [%key:component::meshtastic::issues::migrated_from_custom_integration::title%]
confirm.description:
The configuration for {name} at {host} was taken over from the Meshtastic custom integration that was installed through HACS.

The connection settings were migrated, but the devices and entities of the built-in integration are new ones, so automations, dashboards and history that refer to the old entity IDs need updating. Uninstall the custom integration as well: both would otherwise compete for the node's single client slot.

Select **Submit** once you have done this.

node_unresponsive.title: {name} did not come back after rebooting
node_unresponsive.description:
A configuration change was written to {name} ({node_id}) that makes the node reboot, but {gateway} has not heard from it since.

Check that the node still has power and is in range. This issue disappears on its own as soon as the node is heard again.

export_config.name: Export configuration
export_config.description: Returns the configuration of the connected Meshtastic node, in the shape the Meshtastic command line exports it. The response contains the channel URL, which carries the channel keys, so treat it as a secret. The node's private and administration keys are redacted.

reboot.name: Reboot node
reboot.description: Restarts the Meshtastic node Home Assistant is connected to. The node stops relaying and receiving mesh traffic while it comes back up, which takes about half a minute.

delay.name: Delay
delay.description: How long the node waits before it restarts.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be enabled. Restarting the node interrupts the mesh.

refresh_nodes.name: Refresh node database
refresh_nodes.description: Asks the connected node to send its whole list of known nodes. Use this sparingly: while the list streams, the node can drop received mesh packets, and on a memory-constrained node such as a T-Beam without PSRAM the transfer itself can crash it. Home Assistant learns nodes from live traffic without this.

remove_node.name: Remove node
remove_node.description: Deletes a node from the node database of the connected Meshtastic node. The node is learned again the next time it is heard.

confirm.name: [%key:component::meshtastic::services::reboot::fields::confirm::name%]
confirm.description: Must be enabled. The node is deleted from the node database.

request_position.name: Request position
request_position.description: Asks one mesh node to report where it is and returns the position it answers with. A node answers a position request at most once every three minutes.

node.name: Node
node.description: The mesh node to address, as a node ID such as !aabbccdd, a node number, or a Home Assistant device.

request_telemetry.name: Request telemetry
request_telemetry.description: Asks one mesh node for a telemetry reading and returns the values it answers with.

telemetry_type.name: Telemetry type
telemetry_type.description: Which family of readings to ask for. A node only answers for the sensors it actually has.

request_traceroute.name: Request traceroute
request_traceroute.description: Traces the path a message takes to one mesh node and back, and returns both routes with the signal-to-noise ratio of every hop. The node accepts one traceroute every 30 seconds.

send_message.name: Send message
send_message.description: Sends a text message to one mesh node, or broadcasts it on a channel, and returns the packet ID and whether the mesh confirmed delivery.

config_entry_id.name: Meshtastic node
config_entry_id.description: The Meshtastic node Home Assistant is connected to. Only needed when more than one is set up.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text to send. A Meshtastic packet holds 233 bytes, or 200 bytes for a direct message.

channel.name: Channel
channel.description: The channel index to broadcast on. Ignored when a node is given.

want_ack.name: Request acknowledgment
want_ack.description: Ask the mesh to confirm delivery. Turning this off saves airtime but the action can then no longer tell whether the message arrived.

set_favorite.name: Set favorite
set_favorite.description: Marks a node as a favorite in the node database of the connected node, so that it is never evicted to make room for another one.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Turn off to remove the node from the favorites again.

set_ignored.name: Set ignored
set_ignored.description: Makes the connected node drop every packet it hears from a node, without relaying it.

enabled.name: [%key:component::meshtastic::services::set_favorite::fields::enabled::name%]
enabled.description: Turn off to stop ignoring the node again.
